title: Understanding The Glory, The Word & Power of The King
paragraphs: Then I thought that I might also feel lost, because sometimes you forget why you do what you do, and you don't want to forget why you do what you do. What I mean by that is this. You don't want to forget why we study about the king. We don't want to forget why we're doing it. So, I just want to remind you of a few phrases regarding why we should study monarchy. The message of the Bible is about a king and a kingdom. That is why we must study kings. Secondly, God's goal is to expand his kingdom on earth.

Therefore, we must study what the kingdom is. Thirdly, the incarnation of God was the coming of a king. The wise man says that we have come to look for a king. So it is clear that God sent a king to Earth. He is not a prime minister, nor a mayor, nor a governor. He sent a king. Unfortunately, the purpose of Jesus’ coming was to restore the kings to their kingdom. For this reason, the Bible must be viewed in light of what the kingdom is and what the king is.

God's ultimate goal is to re-establish his kingdom on Earth. I want to read some verses that you might want to quickly put your finger on. Matthew chapter 18, verse 23 says: “ Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.” A very important verse. Matthew 18:23. What is the kingdom of God like? What does it resemble? A king. It is very important to understand the words that Jesus used. Another verse you might want to read or write down is Matthew 22:2.

It says: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding feast for his son. ” The kingdom of God is like a king. Matthew 22:2, “The kingdom of heaven is like a king preparing a feast for his son.” Matthew 25:34, a familiar verse, but I want to repeat it. Then the king will say to those on his right, Jesus said, “The king will say to those on his right, ‘You are blessed by my Father.’” Inherit the kingdom prepared for you since the foundation of the world.

I am reading these texts because I want you to realize that all of Jesus’ references to the Kingdom were about a king and a kingdom. There is no way to understand Jesus, and there is no way to understand the Bible unless you understand what a king is and what a kingdom is. That's why we should study this. Is this clear? Is this clear?

This is extremely important because if you approach the Bible, and I think this is why there is so much confusion in what is called Christianity, it is because everyone brings to the Bible their own concept of what God meant, whereas in reality God has left nothing for your own interpretation. God tells us clearly what the Bible is about. He says, " I am a king, and this concerns my kingdom." Is this clear?

The problem is that if you were not born in the time of kings, you have to go back and study what kings are because that is what God chose to define himself by. Does what I'm saying make sense? This is extremely important because I know how much it means to me personally. I am simply blessed to understand what that means. But I want you to understand why you need to understand what that means. Theologians are not automatically right. This is a heavy statement.

I went to college and studied theology, and what they taught me in college was from the writings of some other authors. Not necessarily from the Bible. Most of what we studied was people's comments on the Bible. One of the most important people we had to study as a requirement was Saint Augustine. In fact, much of our theology is taken from Saint Augustine. Saint Augustine was a Catholic. In all Protestant theological seminaries and all universities that teach theology, you must study St. Augustine.

Now bear in mind that I said Saint Augustine was who? He was a Catholic priest. Therefore, Saint Augustine comes to the Bible from his own perspective and background, and 90% of priests who are trained in seminaries have to read and study this man. And I had to do that too. Therefore, he brings into the Bible his Catholic concepts which we Protestants have adopted as our own theology. Now when I read most of what they asked us to read about the theology of St. Augustine, I did not see any kingdom anywhere in it.

I graduated from university with a degree in theology, and there was no course on the Kingdom of God. Not one. In fact, I don't think we discussed this word in any of our classes. The mere word "kingdom" was never discussed. I have obtained a degree in God. This is what theology means. Theo means God. Logic means study. So theology means the study of God. I studied God, but I never studied the Kingdom. However, the entire Bible is about a king and his kingdom. What does God call himself? king. There is no doubt.

Now there are a few things by which God has defined himself. I think the reason for that is that he knows the nature of those things. For example, God identified himself as a lion. Why? God created the lion, and He knows what the nature of the lion is. Therefore, there are certain attributes of the lion by which God has identified Himself. What is a lion? Brave and courageous. Therefore, the Bible calls Jesus the Lion of Judah. God says that he sits on the throne.

It was the lion who sat on the throne when John saw him. It was not a real animal. He was talking about the qualities he had seen. He saw courage. He saw the audacity. He saw the trust. That's how lions are. Then God also identified himself with another animal, the eagle. He said, " I will carry you as an eagle carries its young." "I will move you like an eagle moves its nest." Thus, God describes himself as an eagle. The eagle is a unique bird. The characteristics of the eagle are very clear.

The eagle is very confident. It is the most powerful bird in the bird kingdom. He has better vision than any other bird. It only eats living organisms. In other words, meat that has been killed fresh. The eagle can fly higher than any other bird and is more powerful. In other words, God identified himself with the qualities possessed by the bird he created. Now, I'm saying this for a reason. Here we find God also defining himself by the title of ruler, called King.

This means that in order to understand God, you must study the attributes of the King. Otherwise, you will miss out on knowing what God looks like. Is this clear? Now, God could have said, “Ah, we have been born a mayor, or perhaps a president or prime minister.” He could have said that, and then we would have had to study prime ministers. But God did not say that. God says he is a king. Therefore, you must study the nature of kingship in order to understand God. Then he says that he came to bring about a kingdom.

He defined his system of government as the Kingdom. He did not know it as a republic or a democracy. Not even with communism or socialism. He could have done that, but he didn't. Rather, he introduced it to the Kingdom. For this reason, it is impossible to understand this Holy Scripture unless you first understand what the King is and what the Kingdom is. Is this clear? That's why we should study this matter.

If you don't do it this way, you will read the Bible, come to your own conclusions, come up with your own personal interpretation, and miss what God meant. This is what the theologians did. They became so engrossed in studying the meanings of words that they forgot what they really meant. They are so committed to studying profound matters that they overlook the natural ones. I don't want to be deep. I just want to be right. I have heard some profound things that are not true, and I have been hearing them recently.

I listen to great preachers giving sermons that make you cheer, but they are not true. It does not convey what God intended. I think that the religious community that includes all of us has become so accustomed to having something that makes us cheer that we get more excited about cheering than about what God intended. We follow God and participate in religious activity for the sake of feeling, not for the sake of conversion. I don't know about you, but I don't want to just get excited. I want to be right.

By the way, I discovered that the older you get, the less time you have to waste. So, you don't want to be wrong. Can I hear Amen? You want to make sure that you live the rest of your years doing the right thing. That is why we must study what God says about it. He says he is a king. Now, I will quickly teach you the qualities or characteristics of a king, and we have dealt with two of them so far. Let me list them for you again, and hopefully we can look at three of them today.

If we are unable to do so, we will continue from here next week. Firstly, kings inherit the kingdom by right of birth. We've already talked about that. This is number one. Kings are born kings. Secondly, kings must be trained in their roles and responsibilities. They need to be trained. We talked about that and that's where we left off last time. But the third thing is that the glory of the king is everything that expresses his nature. All kings have what they call glory.

No, they don't talk about glory when you talk about presidents and prime ministers, you know. I mean, our prime minister doesn't have glory, you know, "the glory of our prime minister". We are not talking about that. We are not talking about the glory of the President of the United States. He has no glory in himself. But when you read the Bible, it repeatedly says "the glory of the King," "the glory." Kings have what they call glory. What is glory? We need to talk about that. And I want to address this issue.

Throughout the Bible you will find these terms, "the word of the king". When the King speaks, it is entirely different from whether President Bush speaks, or Prime Minister Christie in the Bahamas, or anyone else. If Mr. Blair speaks, it does not mean the same thing as when the King speaks. Again, this is important because if you live in the Kingdom of God, you cannot expect that what Jesus says is the same as what the Prime Minister says. It's different. That's why we need to talk about it.

So, let me see if I can turn this thing on. I want you to write this down. Let's talk about the king's glory first. Glory to the King. Now, let's first take up the word "glory" and talk about what it means. The word glory, I think we've all studied it a little. The glory of the king is everything that expresses his nature. Please write this down. The glory of the king is everything that expresses his nature. In other words, the glory of the king is what expresses the nature of the king. What does that mean?

The word glory means the word “ kavod” in Hebrew in the Old Testament, and in the New Testament it is the word “ doxa”. All kings have glory. The word "kabud " means full weight. It means true nature. For something. The word "doxa" means the same thing. It means the true essence of something, what something is in its true form, what something is as it really is. All kings have this.

Therefore, when we talk about the glory of the king and think about our king, our king has a certain nature that is shown in what he does. Let's take a look at the Bible and some texts here. I could show you a thousand of them, but for our purpose, we want to look at two of them. Exodus, Chapter 14, Verses 17 and 18. I will read part of it. He says: “Then the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I am glorified by Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.” Ah, this text, am I doing this correctly?

Can you please change it for me? This doesn't work. Thank you very much. This is a very important verse from the Bible. Now, I'm sure you've read this a thousand times in the Bible. God says, " I will do this to show my glory." Ah, glory has something to do with the nature of the king. What kings do to show their nature is that they work. They either create something or do something, and this reveals their true nature. Kings like to show their true nature through their actions.

This is how kings reveal their true nature. So Jesus said he was a king. This means that he has a certain nature and he shows it through what he does. God says to the people, “ Leave Pharaoh alone. Since Pharaoh wants to be stubborn, I will show Pharaoh My true nature. I will do this through My actions. Have you ever heard the phrase, ‘ Stand and see the salvation of the Lord,’ and sometimes, ‘the glory of the Lord’? Let Me show you My nature.

A king loves to show his nature, and he does this through his actions and deeds. God says, ‘ I will do something to Pharaoh, and then Pharaoh and his people will know My true nature.’ (Psalm 4:2). How long, O people, will you turn My glory into dishonor? How long will you love worthless things and seek false gods? This is a very important statement. God says, ‘You bring shame to My glory when you worship idols.’ You and I were created in God’s image. This means the nature of God.

When you do anything, you are actually reflecting His glory. Anything you do that is not like God or does not represent God is a disgrace to His glory. So God says, ‘Look, I am the King.’” I have made you kings. You must behave in a way that is exactly like me. If it is not like Me, then you bring shame upon My glory. ” And He says this here. He says, if you worship idols, then I worship nothing. I do not worship the things I created.

So why do you take My glory and worship idols with it, bringing shame upon Me by worshipping these idols? Therefore, it is not the nature of God that we should worship the things He created. And so if we do that, we bring shame upon the nature of God. Now, in the Book of Psalms, chapter 8, verse 5, He says: “ You made him a little lower than the angels,” referring to humans, “and crowned him with glory and honor.” This is a very important statement. Oh, please open up with me to this chapter.

I want to explain this, because it is very important, as this is what changed my life in my adolescence when I was beginning to understand God. Psalm 8 is talking about You. It is not talking about God. Psalm 8 begins like this: “ O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.” Then in that psalm, He cries out and says: “ What is man that you are mindful of him and make him your son?” Adam? Verse four: “You care for him.”

You made him a little less than the angels. And you crowned him with what? With glory and honor. Now, I just want to comment on something here. Look at the first verse. You set your glory above the heavens. David is referring to all of creation that he sees, millions of stars and galaxies. And he calls that the glory of God. I am a painter, and sometimes when I find the time in my life, I paint. I have a few paintings that I've done hanging in people's homes.

I went to Tulsa a while ago, and I visited a man's house, and I'd forgotten that I'd given him a painting years ago, and the painting was in the room, and I saw my name on it, and I said, “Oh, I forgot that I painted this.” He told me that people come here and everyone wants to know how I got a painting of Miles Munro. But I had given it to him as a gift years ago. And I think about my own work. When I paint, they call the work of a painter or an artist. They call it his glory.

In other words, I've put my glory on the canvas. My glory is my nature. How I look. That's what I've painted. I've released a part of myself and left it on the canvas. A canvas. David says that's what God did when He created the stars, the moon, and the galaxies. He revealed a part of His nature and left it on the canvas of the universe. So you can know the nature of an artist through their work. That's what David is referring to here. So, the glory of a thing is its nature.

So, whatever the king does, he wants to leave a mark so that you can understand his true nature even before you see him. Is anyone still following along? So, the glory of the king is very important. Glory, the glory of the king, is what he shows through his actions and behavior, which reveal his nature. That is the glory of the king. All kings have that. David says, "You have made us to be your glory." " You crowned us with Your nature." That's the meaning of that verse. You gave us Your full weight.

You placed in our human bodies a treasure that is a part of Your nature. So that when people see us, we remind them of God. This amazes me. Tell your neighbor, " I am the glory of God." Notice that the verse doesn't say, "You are God," does it? Wherever that painting of Mine goes, a part of Me goes with it. In other words, wherever you take My work, I go with it. My glory is in it. And if you take that painting and paint it completely black, the painting is still there under the black paint.

That's the definition of sin. Sin is when human disobedience puts black paint over God's beautiful glory, but it remains hidden beneath it. And when the blood of Jesus comes, it's like turpentine. It washes away all the black paint, and the glory is revealed. That's why when you disobey God, you cover the glory. All kings have glory. Now, another verse I want you to read is Psalm 19: 1. It says, "What do the heavens say?" By the glory of God, and what does the skin tell? By his own hands. "The works of his hands.

Look, he's an artist. God has shown his glory in what he has created. But he also shows his glory in what he does. His actions. What God created is what God has done. His works are what he is doing now. Both show his glory. I remember something that bothered me. And this is still a theological problem for some, although, you know, I don't find it a problem anymore. But there is a problem in theology, especially in charismatic theology, regarding who makes people sick.

Well, everyone thinks it's the devil who makes people sick, and I say no, maybe it's their own actions that made them sick or something like that. Of course, there are some illnesses that are a result of your own negligence. You do n't eat well and you don't take care of yourself. You know your body reacts to that and you get sick. That means you bring the illness upon yourself. But there are also certain illnesses that come into your life.

Maybe you inherit them from your paternal lineage or your DNA and such, and that's something you have no control over. You need to be healed from it. You need a miracle for that. But there was a man who was born blind. If you remember this incident when he healed him..." Jesus, people say, "Do you know why he was blind? Because someone did something evil." And they, you know, people try to find reasons for your illness. They come up with all sorts of explanations. You know, maybe you didn't pay tithes or something.

All sorts of things. You know, whatever you did. And they do all these strange things to try to justify why you were sick. But I remember Jesus amazed me that day. When you read it, it says, " And they began to tell Jesus, ' We know why he was sick.' He was sick because his parents did evil and gossiped and so on." But Jesus stopped them. He said, " No." He said, "This man was born blind so that the glory of God might be displayed." Isn't this amazing?

In other words, God allowed this man's eye to be incomplete at birth so that he could complete it later. God did not want the eye to be completed secretly in the womb because no one could see it. He did not want to see his glory only in the womb. In this case, I believe that God allows you to go through some terrible situations. He allows it to happen while he observes the whole thing. He allows things to proceed in this manner. Why? Because later his glory will appear. I've been through that. I know.

She says, "Oh God, my house is up for sale." They are going to sell my house. "It's in the newspapers." God said, "Let him go." Let him go. "Let him go." Right to the end. He let him go. Then he said, " Now, let me show them who I am." Sometimes you feel, "Oh God, this marriage is about to end." I've tried everything, and God says, " That's right. Just leave it alone. Don't interfere. Just relax." Sometimes God's instruction is to do nothing. And that's the hardest thing to obey.

Does anyone know what I'm talking about? The hardest thing to obey from God is to do nothing. When God says, "Do nothing," it's hard because we always feel like we have to do something to fix things. God said it to Moses many times. He said, "Stand firm." Wow, that's the hardest thing to do in front of God because you always want to do something. Stand firm. And some of you are going through this right now. Some of you are going through things right now, and God is n't telling you anything. Why?

He just wants you to stand firm and see the glory of the Lord. The glory of the Lord. The glory of the Lord is what he is like, his very nature. Now, every king doesn't just do works to show his glory, but his works and the things he has created show his glory. That's why kings build castles. That's why Kings decorate their castles. That's why kings surround themselves with all this extravagance, because the king wants you to meet him before you actually meet him. Come on, guys, pay attention.

I know it's a bit hot, but focus on this. Look, that's why the king is extravagant. He'd put gold leaf on the walls, diamonds on the doorknobs, and I mean, the things you're fighting over, the king walks on. Do you know why? He wants you to be awestruck by the sheer glory of the place itself when you enter it. My God. That's why it's so important to understand the kingdom. Look, God wants to bless you in such a way that when people see you from afar, they immediately recognize, "I know who its king is.

I know who his king is." Let me tell you something. You're about to get into some things. Look, now, let me tell you, it's hard to teach them, man. Let me tell you, okay, listen. The problem with the kingdom, if there is a problem, is that it doesn't work until you believe. The problem with belief is that you can't believe until you know. Is anyone with me? This is very important. Okay. So, the problem is, you can't experience it until you believe it. But you can't believe it until someone tells you.

Because faith comes from what? From hearing. So, there are many things you haven't been able to experience up to this point in your lives because you haven't received this teaching yet. Do you understand? It's very difficult. That's why Jesus went to his hometown, and the Bible says he had the power to heal everyone. It says, "But he could not because of their unbelief."

In other words, even though the power to make you rich and prosperous to represent God is there, it can't be realized until you connect with it and believe that you are meant to be. So, we can't blame God for our poverty. We have to blame our ignorance at the moment. But tell your neighbor, "I'm getting out of that right now." Say it out loud. "I'm getting out of that right now." See, when your mind changes, your life changes.

So, what I'm saying to you is this: If He is the King and you are His glory, let me explain who you are. You are His ornament. You are slow, man. This Good place to shout. So your flourishing is necessary for God to show what he looks like, because He is a God of unlimited wealth and power, and that's what you're meant to show. Tell your neighbor, "I must flourish. For His reputation." Clap your hands. Praise God. "I must flourish for His reputation." The Bible says the heavens proclaim it. Whenever you think God is poor, go and walk in the wilderness and see how God made those plants you pay for grow wild.

I'll never forget seeing wildflowers everywhere on the street that day in Nebraska, and we pay $10 for one. His glory places them everywhere. Go and walk on the beach. At five in the morning, watch the sunrise. Go alone, and let the Lord observe for a few minutes and challenge you to draw it if you are skilled. In fact, He challenges you to photograph it.

The moment you photograph it, the image becomes worthless because it has changed. His beauty, His glory, and what He looks like are all around. Paul says that if a person has never encountered God, they have no excuse because God speaks to them through nature. God tells you who He is like through His work. Can I hear an Amen? Yes. I must add this point. This is a nice, small one. The glory of God is shown in your straightness. It is an exit, not an entrance. That is the glory in that.

Praise be to God. The Mighty and Powerful. The Lord Almighty in battle. He is the King of Glory. Wow. I just want to stay there for a few weeks and preach.

Now, do you know who is writing this? A king. David is the richest king in the world because his son is not yet king. His son has become richer than he was or is. But here King David is talking about another king. David says, 'I know when I go in, that I am a great person there.'" I have my glory."

This verse made me shout that day. Psalm 96. Quickly, quickly, quickly. The third verse. She says: " Speak of his glory." Psalm 96: 3 Tell of his glory among the nations. Let them see what it's like on your university campus. In fact, when people look at you, they should mistake you for God. They should say, "Did God come to the school today?" You begin to represent his nature wherever you go. But I love this part.

He says here, not only should you bring him before the nations, but he says, his deeds must show among the people what he is like. This is what kings want. They want to be represented. John 8:54. Please turn to the New Testament quickly. John 8:54. Jesus answered, " If I glorify myself, my glory is worth nothing." My Father, whom you call your God, is the one who glorifies me. Hallelujah. Again, in John chapter 8, verse 54, Jesus said: If I glorify myself, my glory is worth nothing.

This means that if I give you a piece of my mind, it means nothing. But if I glorify my father through what I do, he says that this is what the father wants. If we are representing the King of Kings as kings, then everything we do, everything we say, and how we live is supposed to represent how King Jesus is. Otherwise, we bring shame upon his glory. Look at John 17 a few pages later from there. John Chapter 17 Verse 4. I have glorified you on earth by completing the work that you gave me to do.

How do you glorify God? By completing the work he gave you to do. How do you glorify God? By actually doing something with your life. To produce something in your life from what is inside you. This is how God is glorified. You show how our King is by producing what He has put into you. Therefore, glorifying God is not really about singing, clapping, dancing, and all those things in church service.

Rather, it is what you do when you leave that celebratory experience and go out and produce your life as a secretary, or as a mechanic, or as a plumber, or as a maintenance technician, whatever your job may be. When you go out to work, you demonstrate its qualities through your work. If you drive a taxi, you are supposed to be the most glorious taxi driver in the Bahamas. I need a vision about who you are and who I am. If you are the glory of God and I am the glory of God, then I will love you as I love God. Amen.
